# A canonical selected star has a quadratic joint escape

The canonical selected group in
candidate 9b703b460ed5bf2b admits a
stronger escape than its cubic path. The endpoint and cap parameters
can both move to first order, with zero first variation of every
selected global cap and of total volume. Their joint Lagrangian has
an explicit positive second variation. A physical acceleration then
increases total volume and strictly decreases all retained cap masses
to second order.

This is a statement about actual global cap budgets, with one endpoint
free and the other two fibers fixed. It is not a stationarity theorem
for arbitrary simultaneous changes of all fibers or an OC conclusion.

## 1. Actual model and a smooth joint problem

Fix \(d\ge2\), \(m=d+1\), and a centered full-dimensional \(d\)-simplex
\(K\), of volume \(V\), with barycentric coordinates
\(\lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m\), \(0\le i\le d\).
The actual three fibers at bases \(-1,0,1\) are
\[
 K(W),\quad K-K,\quad -K.
\]
Here the columns of \(W\), whose column sums are one, are the
barycentric vertex coordinates of the moving endpoint. Write
\(U=|K-K|\), \(M=2V+U\), \(D=V+U/2\), and
\(\Gamma=(d/m)^d\).

For a proper vector \(a\), with \(\sum a_i=1\), retain the single group
\[
 H_i(a)=\{l_i(x)+(a_i-1/m)z\ge0\}.
\]
Its margins sum to zero, so it covers the whole ambient space.
Put
\[
 P_i(W,a)=\frac{F_i(W,a)}V
 =\det W\,\frac{(W_{ii}-a_i)^d}
                  {\prod_{j\ne i}(W_{ii}-W_{ij})}.
\]
These formulas are analytic on one common neighborhood of
\((I,a^*)\), \(a^*=m^{-1}{\bf1}\). The exact normalized global cap
increments are
\[
 c_i(W,a)=\frac{\mu_W(H_i(a))-D}{V}
         =P_i(W,a)-P_i(I,a).                         \tag{1}
\]
In particular \(c_i(I,a)=0\) identically. The dependence of the
unchanged reflected endpoint on the moving cap parameter is included
in (1).

The source note proves that all sufficiently small physical \(W-I\)
preserve the actual three integer fibers: the forced middle
Minkowski average remains compactly inside \(K-K\). We use that open
compatibility neighborhood throughout.

## 2. The canonical first stress and a critical velocity

For a physical velocity \(B\), with zero column sums, let
\[
 T=\operatorname{tr}B,\quad b_i=B_{ii},\quad
 s_i=\sum_{j\ne i}B_{ij}.
\]
At \(a^*\), the normalized cap derivative is
\[
 f_i(B)=D_Wc_i(I,a^*)[B]=\Gamma(T+s_i+b_i).           \tag{2}
\]
The threshold derivative is zero by (1). The map \(f\) is onto:
given \(f\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(z_i=f_i/(m\Gamma)\), \(Z=\sum z_i\),
and the physical matrix
\[
 S(f)_{ii}=z_i,\qquad S(f)_{ij}=z_i-Z/d\quad(i\ne j).
                                                               \tag{3}
\]
Then \(f(S(f))=f\), and \(\operatorname{tr}S(f)=\sum f_i/(m\Gamma)\).
Thus the joint smooth constraint system admits a strictly feasible
linearized direction. Its positive objective-one first stress is
\(\ell_i=1/(m\Gamma)\). The normalized Lagrangian is
\[
 {\cal L}(W,a)=\det W-\frac1{m\Gamma}\sum_i c_i(W,a). \tag{4}
\]
Its full first derivative vanishes at \((I,a^*)\).

Take \(E_{01}=1\), \(E_{11}=-1\), all other entries zero, and put
\[
 B=E-S(f(E)),\qquad \omega=e_1-e_0.                 \tag{5}
\]
Then \(f(B)=0\), \(T=0\), and \(\sum\omega_i=0\). Hence \((B,\omega)\)
is a critical joint velocity for every individual cap constraint.
Explicitly,
\[
 b_0=0,\qquad b_1=-\frac{d-1}{m},\qquad
 b_i=\frac1m\quad(2\le i\le d).
\]
The off-diagonal entries are
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 B_{01}=(d-1)/d,& B_{0j}=-1/d\quad(j\ge2),\\
 B_{1j}=(d-1)/(md)&(j\ne1),\\
 B_{ij}=-1/(md)&(i\ge2,\ j\ne i).
 \end{array}                                                   \tag{6}
\]
These also directly verify zero column sums, \(s_i=-b_i\), and
\[
 \sum_i b_i^2=\frac{d(d-1)}{m^2},\quad
 \sum_{i\ne j}B_{ij}^2=\frac{d-1}{d}+\frac{d-1}{m^2},\quad
 b\cdot\omega=-\frac{d-1}{m}.                       \tag{7}
\]

## 3. Exact positive joint Hessian

Let \(\sigma=\operatorname{tr}(B^2)\) and
\[
 R_i=\sum_{j\ne i}(b_i-B_{ij})^2.
\]
Since each first derivative in (2) vanishes, differentiating the
logarithm of the proper-cap formula gives
\[
 D^2_{WW}P_i(I,a^*)[B,B]
   =\Gamma\left[-\sigma-\frac{m^2}{d}b_i^2+R_i\right].          \tag{8}
\]
The mixed derivative follows either from the same formula or by
differentiating the general first derivative in \(a_i\):
\[
 D_aD_WP_i(I,a^*)[B,\omega]
       =\Gamma\frac{m^2}{d}b_i\omega_i.                        \tag{9}
\]
The factor arising from differentiation of \((1-a_i)^d\) multiplies
the zero first derivative and disappears. The pure \(aa\) block of
every \(c_i\), and therefore of \({\cal L}\), vanishes identically
by (1).

Equations (8) and (4) give
\[
 D^2_{WW}{\cal L}[B,B]
 =\frac md\sum b_i^2-\frac1m\sum R_i
 =-\frac{d-1}{dm}.                                          \tag{10}
\]
For the second equality use \(s_i=-b_i\), which gives
\(\sum R_i=(d+2)\sum b_i^2+\sum_{i\ne j}B_{ij}^2\), then (7).
The mixed block is
\[
 D_aD_W{\cal L}[B,\omega]=-\frac md b\cdot\omega
                       =\frac{d-1}{d}.                      \tag{11}
\]
Consequently the exact joint critical Hessian is
\[
 Q:=D^2{\cal L}[(B,\omega),(B,\omega)]
   =\frac{d-1}{d}\left(2-\frac1m\right)>0.                    \tag{12}
\]
This displays the missing mixed contribution directly. The negative
fixed-threshold value (10) does not control the joint problem. The
first stress remains valid and positive, but its joint second-order
necessary condition fails.

## 4. Explicit acceleration pays every cap

The second derivative of the normalized global cap increment on the
straight critical path is, by (8)-(9),
\[
 q_i=\Gamma\left[-\sigma-\frac{m^2}{d}b_i^2+R_i
                    +\frac{2m^2}{d}b_i\omega_i\right].       \tag{13}
\]
The pure threshold terms have canceled; dropping the reflected
endpoint would change this formula.
The volume second derivative is \(q_V=-\sigma\), and (12) says
\[
 q_V-\frac1{m\Gamma}\sum_i q_i=Q.                             \tag{14}
\]
Choose
\[
 \epsilon=\frac{\Gamma Q}{2},\qquad
 C=S(-q-\epsilon{\bf1}),\qquad
 W(t)=I+tB+\frac{t^2}{2}C,\quad a(t)=a^*+t\omega.             \tag{15}
\]
Both physical matrices in (15) have zero column sums. Formula (3)
makes every individual cap's second derivative equal to \(-\epsilon\),
whereas (14) makes the volume second derivative \(Q/2\).
Thus the actual mixed mass and every retained global cap satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 M(t)&=M+\frac{VQ}{4}t^2+O(t^3),\\
 \mu_t(H_i(a(t)))&=D-\frac{V\Gamma Q}{4}t^2+O(t^3).
 \end{split}                                                 \tag{16}
\]
All leading coefficients have the required strict signs. Analyticity
on the common proper-cap neighborhood gives one remainder bound for
the finite family. For all sufficiently small positive \(t\), (15)
preserves exact convex compatibility, the proper cut pattern, and
the full-space group cover, while strictly improving every budget.
This is an actual feasible path; no second-order multiplier theorem
is needed to infer its existence.

For example in \(d=2\), \(Q=5/6\), \(\Gamma=4/9\).
The normalized volume gain is \(5t^2/24+O(t^3)\), and every
normalized global cap increment is \(-5t^2/54+O(t^3)\).

## 5. Binary isolation and limitations

The finite binary isolation construction in the selected-star note
applies unchanged to (15). Its strict margins persist on this path.
The retained star caps decrease, all regular cap masses stay exactly
\(D\), and every actual integer fiber stays covered. The regular
simplex centroids keep absolute maximum depth exactly \(D\), while
total mass gains the amount in (16). In the three-fiber star alone,
the selected cover bounds the new absolute maximum strictly below
\(D\).

The construction changes only one endpoint and the retained group's
base coefficients. It does not claim to preserve the discarded
redundant groups' budgets, remove general compatibility constraints,
or exclude arbitrary globally stationary cap families. In particular
it is compatible with the fixed-body cancellation of every through-
origin cap's first normal derivative on the symmetric star.

The companion verifier checks the identities and exact rational paths.
The proof above establishes all \(d\ge2\), independently of the
finite dimensions checked computationally.

## 6. Any centrally symmetric source with a free off-center simplex

The same calculation applies in any integer dimension \(n\ge1\).
Let an actual finite-fiber mixed source, arising from a compact convex
body and of intrinsic continuous dimension \(d\ge2\), be centrally
symmetric about \((0,0)\). Ignore
its zero \(d\)-volume fibers in the measure, but retain actual
convex compatibility. Suppose a positive fiber at an integer base
\(p\ne0\) is a full \(d\)-simplex and is **freely variable** in the
following precise sense: every sufficiently small labeled affine
vertex perturbation of this one fiber, with all other positive fibers
fixed, is realizable by an actual convex body with exactly those
positive fibers and no additional positive integer fibers.
This open feasibility assumption is not deduced merely from symmetry.

Its reflected fiber at \(-p\) is then the reflected simplex. Choose
any real base functional \(v\) satisfying \(v\cdot p=1\), and let \(c\)
be the simplex centroid at \(p\). The lattice-base-preserving shear
\[
 (z,x)\longmapsto (z,x-c(v\cdot z))
\]
centers the simplex and its reflected mate simultaneously, commutes
with central reflection, and has continuous fiber Jacobian one.
No integrality of \(v\) is needed: the integer base is unchanged.
Write the resulting centered simplex as \(K\), with the same
barycentric coordinates used above.

For any proper concurrent \(a\), choose the ambient caps
\[
 H_i(a)=
 \{l_i(x)-(a_i-1/m)(v\cdot z)\ge0\}.                \tag{17}
\]
At \(p\), (17) is \(\lambda_i\ge a_i\); at \(-p\), reflection
converts it to \(\lambda_i\le a_i\) on \(K\). Every cap is nonvertical,
its boundary is null for the \(d\)-dimensional mixed measure, and its
boundary passes through the symmetry center. Therefore its mass on
the entire unchanged original source is exactly \(D=M/2\), for every
nearby \(a\). The other reflected fibers may each change their cap
masses as \(a\) varies; only their complete original-source sum is
being asserted constant.

Perturb just the fiber at \(p\). Its exact global cap increment is
again
\[
 \mu_W(H_i(a))-D=F_i(W,a)-F_i(I,a).
                                                               \tag{18}
\]
Thus all derivatives, the positive joint Hessian (12), and the
physical acceleration (15) transfer without alteration. The explicit
free-fiber hypothesis supplies compatibility. The margins in (17)
sum to zero throughout, so the caps cover the entire ambient space.
Consequently (16) holds, and the actual maximum absolute depth of
the perturbed source is strictly less than its original \(M/2\).

The original source already has depth \(M/2\) at its symmetry center:
nonvertical through-origin caps split its mass, and vertical closed
caps have at least half its mass. The center is an actual mixed point
by convexity and symmetry, and a nonvertical opposite pair gives the
matching global upper bound. Hence this extension concerns a
symmetric, OC-safe source and the stability of its selected cover.
It does not supply a new below-OC exclusion or make an arbitrary
off-center simplex freely variable.
